newsitem.title: USA: PRESS DIGEST - New York Times business - March 4.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - New York Times business - March 4.

text.p: The New York Times reported the following business stories on Tuesday:

* A four-month takeover battle for Conrail may be nearing an end, as Conrail appears close to reaching a $10.3 billion pact with CSX and Norfolk Southern that would split Conrail's lines between its suitors.
* New AT&T President John Walter sent the company's stock reeling after telling analysts he foresees increased costs and competition further draining already sluggish profits.

* With the Dow industrials and stock prices hovering near record highs, experts say this could be one of the biggest years ever for stock splits. So far this year Boeing, DuPont, Exxon, IBM and Philip Morris have all announced splits, and Intel, BankAmerica and Bristol-Myers Squibb are among those scheduling splits.

* Northeast Utilities said it is suing the New Hampshire Public Utilities Commission to block a state deregulation plan that it says could cut its revenue by $341 million and eventually drive it into bankruptcy.

* Concerns that the Federal Reserve would raise interest rates rose after the National Association of Purchasing Managers reported that manufacturing activity was up and after the Commerce Department said personal income increased.
* UAL's United Airlines and its pilots' and machinists' union reached a tentative agreement providing for the largest possible salary and benefit gains allowed under an arbiter's ruling.
* Ameritech and AT&T said they agreed to settle three legal disputes between them but did not disclose terms of the settlements.
* Sales for Chrysler fell three percent in February, and those for General Motors fell 7.5 percent.
* The Dow industrials ended three days of losses and rose 41.18 points to 6,918.92, propelled by DuPont.
* The 30-year bond yield rose to 6.83 percent from 6.80.

* China's exports rose to $151 billion in 1996, a thirtyfold increase in 20 years, and during some months last year, China surpassed Japan as the country with the greatest trade surplus with the United States.
* Westinghouse's CBS is negotiating to buy a one-third stake in the on-line sports service called Sportsline USA Inc for $100 million, people familiar with the matter say.
* The Mexican Government has charged Carlos Peralta Quintero, a partner in a cellular-telephone venture with Bell Atlantic, with criminal tax fraud.

* U.S. Commerce Secretary William Daley overhauled rules governing American trade missions abroad to try to insure that companies that donate heavily to political campaigns do not get special help breaking into foreign markets.
* HFS agreed to buy Value Rent-a-Car from Mitsubishi Motor Sales of America for $175 million in cash.
